# Requirements Analysis Document — draft template

1. Project purpose: reusable engine plus separate demonstration game.
2. Target users and representative use cases.
3. Scope: required vs optional engine/game features.
4. Inputs, outputs, configuration and supported platforms.
5. Functional requirements: ID, behavior, owner, acceptance criteria, Jira link.
6. Nonfunctional requirements: measured performance/reliability/usability targets.
7. GUI sketches, navigation, gameplay parameters and agreed multiplayer rules.
8. Team responsibilities and dependencies.
9. Sprint plan, progress evidence, unresolved questions and risks.
10. Traceability: requirement → Jira → implementation → test.

Fill from reviewed team decisions; do not present starter placeholders as delivered requirements.

## Current demonstration scope to expand

Two human-controlled elemental characters cooperate in puzzle rooms. Describe movement/jump inputs, visual/audio outputs, matching hazards/exits, linked pressure plates/doors and shared restart. Separate local co-op from the networked session deliverable.

For each functional requirement include acceptance criteria and a Jira owner. Example: both living characters must reach their matching exits in the same step; one character alone cannot complete the room. List gravity, movement/jump speed, character/collider dimensions and room spacing as playability parameters.

Create sketches for title, local/host/join selection, character assignment, gameplay HUD, pause/settings, shared failure/restart and level-complete screens. Show navigation arrows. Record at least one actual sprint in progress with time estimates when the RAD is submitted; do not substitute this template for Jira evidence.
